about: Cognitive pressures a bounded fiction may place on a participant who chose to enter it. This is literary vocabulary for voluntary experiences, not guidance for influencing real people. Extensible: add entries rather than stretching existing ones.

entries.name: Attention
entries.gloss: What the participant attends to shapes what they later believe happened. Something important can sit in plain view while attention is held elsewhere.

entries.name: Salience
entries.gloss: Vivid, emotional or recent details feel more important than quiet ones, whatever their actual weight.

entries.name: Inference
entries.gloss: The participant fills gaps with conclusions that feel observed but were supplied by their own reasoning.

entries.name: Anchoring
entries.gloss: An early number, claim or impression becomes the reference point later judgments adjust from, usually too little.

entries.name: Framing
entries.gloss: The same facts lead to different judgments depending on how they are presented: as gain or loss, danger or opportunity, duty or choice.

entries.name: Availability
entries.gloss: What comes easily to mind feels common or likely.

entries.name: Representativeness
entries.gloss: Something that resembles a familiar type is taken to be that type, even when the resemblance is superficial.

entries.name: Base-rate neglect
entries.gloss: A vivid particular case overrides quiet background facts about how often things are actually so.

entries.name: Causal attribution
entries.gloss: Outcomes get explained by character and intention when circumstance did more of the work, or the reverse.

entries.name: Confirmation
entries.gloss: The participant looks for, notices and remembers what supports the account they already hold.

entries.name: Belief perseverance
entries.gloss: A belief survives after the evidence that created it has been taken away.

entries.name: Motivated reasoning
entries.gloss: Reasoning bends toward the conclusion the participant wants, while feeling like neutral analysis.

entries.name: Cognitive dissonance
entries.gloss: When action and belief conflict, one of them quietly changes to restore consistency.

entries.name: Identity protection
entries.gloss: Evidence that threatens who the participant takes themselves to be meets more resistance than evidence that is merely inconvenient.

entries.name: Sunk cost
entries.gloss: What has already been spent, given or endured makes continuing feel necessary.

entries.name: Authority
entries.gloss: Claims gain weight from the standing, credentials, uniform or confidence of whoever makes them.

entries.name: Conformity
entries.gloss: The participant's judgments drift toward those of the group around them.

entries.name: Pluralistic ignorance
entries.gloss: Everyone privately doubts something while each assumes the others believe it.

entries.name: Social proof
entries.gloss: What others appear to be doing becomes evidence of what is right or safe to do.

entries.name: Reciprocity
entries.gloss: A gift, favor or disclosure creates a felt obligation to return it.

entries.name: Commitment
entries.gloss: Having said or done something small makes a larger, consistent step feel natural.

entries.name: Scarcity
entries.gloss: Something rare, closing or contested becomes more desirable.

entries.name: Loss aversion
entries.gloss: Losing something weighs more than gaining the same thing, so avoiding loss drives choices.

entries.name: Endowment
entries.gloss: What the participant holds, or has come to think of as theirs, becomes worth more to them.

entries.name: Status quo
entries.gloss: The current arrangement feels like the safe default even when change would serve better.

entries.name: Omission
entries.gloss: What goes unsaid shapes belief as powerfully as what is said, and harm by inaction feels lighter than harm by action.

entries.name: Semantic priming
entries.gloss: Words and images met earlier tilt how later ambiguous things are read.
entries.caution: Evidence for strong behavioral priming effects is weak. Treat this as texture, not as a lever.

entries.name: Presupposition
entries.gloss: A question or statement carries an assumption the participant accepts without examining it.

entries.name: Category construction
entries.gloss: The categories used to sort the world decide what can be seen and what counts as the same kind of thing.

entries.name: Narrative coherence
entries.gloss: A story that hangs together feels true, and gaps get filled to keep it hanging together.

entries.name: Teleology
entries.gloss: Things are read as existing for a purpose, and events as heading toward an intended end.

entries.name: Hindsight
entries.gloss: Once an outcome is known, it seems to have been predictable all along.

entries.name: Illusion of explanatory depth
entries.gloss: The participant feels they understand how something works until they have to explain it.

entries.name: Overconfidence
entries.gloss: Certainty runs ahead of accuracy.

entries.name: Information asymmetry
entries.gloss: Some parties know what others don't, and the difference shapes every exchange between them.

entries.name: Signaling
entries.gloss: Costly or visible actions stand in for qualities that can't be observed directly, and they can be imitated.

entries.name: Principal-agent problem
entries.gloss: Someone acting on another's behalf has interests of their own that the other can't fully see or control.

entries.name: Adversarial incentives
entries.gloss: Another party gains when the participant is wrong, and behaves accordingly.
